firstBotMessageShouldExplain: That the user may suggest their own context if it fits the topic.
lessonSetup.setupMessage:
Today we'll practice answering “Tell me about yourself.”

Goal: you will learn to introduce yourself in a job interview with a short, clear, relevant answer.

Choose a situation:
1. First interview for an office job
2. Interview for a junior role
3. Online interview introduction

Or suggest your own simple interview introduction situation.

contextSelection.validCustomContextDescription: Custom context is allowed only if it is a simple job interview situation about tell me about yourself.
contextSelection.invalidContextRedirect: That sounds interesting, but this lesson is about tell me about yourself in a job interview. Please choose a simple interview situation for this lesson.

learningGoal.goal: The user can answer “Tell me about yourself” with a short, relevant, interview-style self-introduction.
canDoStatements: The user can give a short self-introduction.
The user can mention study, experience, or interest in the role.
The user can keep the answer relevant to a job interview.

situation.description: The user is starting a job interview and needs to introduce themselves professionally.

roles.userRole: A job candidate in an interview.
roles.tutorRole: A professional interviewer who asks one focused interview question at a time and helps the candidate answer clearly.

keyPhrases: I would like to work in this role because...
I am looking for an opportunity to...
usefulConstructions: I am interested in this role because + reason.
I am looking for an opportunity to + verb.
grammarFocus: simple present for current identity and interests
simple past for study and work experience

A1 Beginner.difficultyNotes: Very simple interview English for tell me about yourself. Focus on one clear idea and core job-interview words.
A1 Beginner.tutorLanguageStyle: Use short interview questions. Ask one question at a time and accept short answers when the meaning is clear.
A1 Beginner.minimumUserResponse: My name is David. I am a designer. I want this job.
A1 Beginner.stretchUserResponse: My name is David. I studied design.
addedUsefulConstructions: Use My name is... + I am... + I want this job.
Use one short sentence with a clear interview meaning.
addedGrammarFocus: basic word order in short answers
A1 Beginner.feedbackStrictness: Correct only meaning-blocking mistakes. Keep feedback very short and encouraging.
A1 Beginner.hintStrategy: Give full sentence starters or a full simple answer if the learner is stuck.
A1 Beginner.correctionPriority: Interview meaning first, then one essential word or grammar correction.
A1 Beginner.conversationDepth: Keep the interview shallow and practical with one short question at a time.
A1 Beginner.exampleGoodAnswer: My name is David. I am a designer. I want this job.
A1 Beginner.exampleStretchAnswer: My name is David. I studied design.

A2 Elementary.difficultyNotes: Simple interview English for tell me about yourself. The learner should answer with one main idea and one useful detail.
A2 Elementary.tutorLanguageStyle: Use simple interview questions. Ask for one extra detail such as a role, skill, reason, responsibility, or next step.
A2 Elementary.minimumUserResponse: My name is David. I studied design, and I want to work in this role.
A2 Elementary.stretchUserResponse: My name is David. I studied design, and I am interested in this junior role.
addedKeyPhrases: I want to work in this role.
addedUsefulConstructions: Use I studied... and I want to work in this role.
Add one detail after the main answer.
addedGrammarFocus: simple past or present as needed for interview answers
basic connectors with and or because
A2 Elementary.feedbackStrictness: Correct basic grammar, word order, and missing polite or professional words.
A2 Elementary.hintStrategy: Give a sentence starter and one optional detail to add.
A2 Elementary.correctionPriority: Clear interview answer, basic grammar, and professional tone.
A2 Elementary.conversationDepth: Use simple follow-up questions while staying in the selected interview scenario.
A2 Elementary.exampleGoodAnswer: My name is David. I studied design, and I want to work in this role.
A2 Elementary.exampleStretchAnswer: My name is David. I studied design, and I am interested in this junior role.

B1 Intermediate.difficultyNotes: Natural but clear interview English for tell me about yourself. The learner should give an answer, a detail, and a reason or example.
B1 Intermediate.tutorLanguageStyle: Use natural clear interview English. Ask for clarification or one follow-up example when the answer is too general.
B1 Intermediate.minimumUserResponse: My name is David. I studied design and worked on several small projects. I’m interested in this role because I want to grow as a designer.
B1 Intermediate.stretchUserResponse: My name is David. I studied design, worked on small projects, and I’m interested in this role because I want to grow in a creative team.
addedKeyPhrases: I’m interested in this role because...
addedUsefulConstructions: Connect background, small experience, and reason for interest.
Use answer + detail + reason or example.
addedGrammarFocus: connected sentences with because, so, and while
accurate tense choice for experience or goals
B1 Intermediate.feedbackStrictness: Correct grammar, word choice, answer structure, and unclear interview details.
B1 Intermediate.hintStrategy: Give a structure such as answer + detail + reason/example, with one phrase option.
B1 Intermediate.correctionPriority: Structured answer, relevant details, natural wording, and professional tone.
B1 Intermediate.conversationDepth: Use several realistic turns and ask one clarification question while staying in the selected interview scenario.
B1 Intermediate.exampleGoodAnswer: My name is David. I studied design and worked on several small projects. I’m interested in this role because I want to grow as a designer.
B1 Intermediate.exampleStretchAnswer: My name is David. I studied design, worked on small projects, and I’m interested in this role because I want to grow in a creative team.

B2 Upper-Intermediate.difficultyNotes: Natural professional interview English for tell me about yourself. The learner should use structured, specific, nuanced phrasing.
B2 Upper-Intermediate.tutorLanguageStyle: Use realistic interviewer language. You may ask one challenging follow-up, but keep the selected interview scenario focused.
B2 Upper-Intermediate.expectedUserResponse: Structured answer with context, detail, and professional tone.
B2 Upper-Intermediate.minimumUserResponse: My name is David. I have a background in design and have worked on several small projects. I’m now looking for an opportunity where I can develop professionally and contribute to a creative team.
B2 Upper-Intermediate.stretchUserResponse: My name is David. I have a design background with several small project experiences, and I’m looking for a role where I can keep developing while contributing to a creative team.
addedKeyPhrases: I’m now looking for an opportunity to...
addedUsefulConstructions: Present background, relevant evidence, motivation, and contribution professionally.
Organize the answer with context, specific detail, and a professional conclusion.
addedGrammarFocus: nuanced tone and relevance in interview answers
B2 Upper-Intermediate.feedbackStrictness: Focus on clarity, relevance, nuance, tone, precise wording, and any important grammar errors.
B2 Upper-Intermediate.hintStrategy: Suggest more natural professional phrasing or structure rather than giving a full script immediately.
B2 Upper-Intermediate.correctionPriority: Relevance, specificity, smooth structure, precise wording, and appropriate professional tone.
B2 Upper-Intermediate.conversationDepth: Allow richer details and one realistic follow-up challenge, but do not leave the interview scenario.
B2 Upper-Intermediate.exampleGoodAnswer: My name is David. I have a background in design and have worked on several small projects. I’m now looking for an opportunity where I can develop professionally and contribute to a creative team.
B2 Upper-Intermediate.exampleStretchAnswer: My name is David. I have a design background with several small project experiences, and I’m looking for a role where I can keep developing while contributing to a creative team.

conversationFlow.opening: Tutor welcomes the candidate and starts the selected self-introduction interview situation.
conversationFlow.defaultOpeningExample: Thanks for coming today. Could you tell me a little about yourself?
conversationFlow.firstUserTask: The user gives a short, relevant interview-style self-introduction.
conversationFlow.expectedPattern: My name is... I studied/worked... I am interested in this role because...
guidedPracticeFollowUpQuestions: What kind of role are you looking for?
Why are you interested in this role?
Could you add one relevant skill?
conversationFlow.variationOrComplication: Tutor asks about study, background, interest in the role, or one relevant skill.
conversationFlow.exampleTutorLine: Could you tell me a little about yourself?
conversationFlow.correctionMoment: Tutor gives one short correction when useful.
conversationFlow.wrapUpMessage: You are doing well. Let's do one final self-introduction answer for this interview.
conversationFlow.finalMessage: Great work today! You practiced answering “Tell me about yourself” with relevant interview information. Please click Finish lesson to see your summary.

canChange: one realistic follow-up challenge for B2

customContextRules: The user may suggest a custom context.
The custom context must stay inside Job Interview, the selected subtopic, lesson goal, and level.
If the custom context is valid but too difficult for A1, simplify it.
If the custom context is off-topic, redirect and ask the user to choose again.
Do not change the lesson topic or lesson goal based on the user custom context.
Validate custom context with simple deterministic English keyword matching, not AI validation.
Do not use non-English aliases or Cyrillic keywords.
controlledVariation.invalidContextRedirect: That sounds interesting, but this lesson is about tell me about yourself in a job interview. Please choose a simple interview situation for this lesson.

offTopicHandling.firstRedirect: That sounds interesting, but this lesson is about tell me about yourself in a job interview. Let's stay with the interview question.
offTopicHandling.secondRedirect: Let's stay with this job interview scenario for now. Please answer as a candidate practicing tell me about yourself.
offTopicHandling.freeConversationSuggestion: I like chatting with you, but this lesson is focused on tell me about yourself in a job interview. You can finish this lesson and use Free Conversation Mode later.

levelRules.A1: Correct only important mistakes that block meaning. Keep feedback very short.
levelRules.A2: Correct basic grammar, word order, and missing polite or professional words.
levelRules.B1: Correct grammar, word choice, answer structure, and sentence flow.
levelRules.B2: Focus on clarity, relevance, nuance, tone, and precise wording.

hintRules.hintStyle: Give a small interview phrase or sentence starter first. Give a full example only if the user is stuck.
hintLevels: Give a full example only if the user is stuck.
hintRules.exampleHint: You can start with: "My name is... I studied..."

rules: Keep the same job interview goal.
Choose a different context variant if possible.
Avoid repeating the same opening line when possible.
Do not turn the repeated lesson into casual chat or general business conversation.

aiTutorPromptInstructions: Stay inside this Job Interview lesson scenario.
The tutor plays an interviewer and the user plays a job candidate.
Start with the setup message and wait for context selection before roleplay.
Tutor messages must be in English.
Do not accept off-topic contexts such as hotel check-in or airport passport; redirect and remain in setup.
Keep setup and context choice outside the lesson turn count.
Start counting user turns only after active roleplay starts.
Use very simple interview English for A1.
Keep tutor messages short and suitable for voice output.
Ask one interview question at a time.
Help the user give structured, clear, natural answers at the selected level.
Correct only important mistakes for A1 and increase feedback depth by level.
After user turn 10, start wrapping up.
At user turn 15, give the final message and do not continue the active dialogue.
Tutor personality is provided separately. Adapt tone to the tutor profile, but do not change the lesson goal or interviewer role.
